desc: PLAN-APPROVED BUT BLOCKED by 096/106/107: no reviewed composed host-link artifact exists. When those gates pass, perform the proven HPM transition, hold host state through eUSB2/ATC/DART/xHCI enumeration, then execute the proved rollback. Passive memory stick only. Pass = expected USB child persists 10 seconds, right DART/xHCI healthy, console responsive, no internal NVMe. No block-sector read, mount, or write. Stop/rollback on fault, role/power mismatch, lost console, or missing child. Requires exact hashes, independent PASS, healthy rig/recovery checklist, and lease. STAGED 2026-08-04 (claude). CJ has pre-approved the enumeration step and has physically inserted a USB stick labelled S128 (128 GB, exFAT) in the RIGHT port. Rig is SERIALIZED for fable's ticket 230, so this runs only after 230 lands -- see docs/COORDINATION.md. NO NEW BUILD NEEDED: use the surviving Image-macsmc-hid-type-fix-nbcon-ppp-usb2-native-right (verified to contain pcie-apple and macsmc, so it passes the boot-dcuart kernel guard) with t6040-j614s-dcuart-wifi-usb2-native-right.dtb and the current initramfs-sdroot-hardened.cpio.gz at maxcpus=1, via IMAGE=<name> on t6040-boot-dcuart.sh. EXPECTATION, set honestly: a bus-powered stick needs VBUS, and ticket 231 established that T6040's PD controllers are SPMI 'usbc,sn201202x,spmi' with NO driver in the tree, so the most likely outcome is a repeat of the 2026-07-21 result -- xHCI root hubs up, no child device. That is still worth running for two reasons: it re-confirms the blocker against a current kernel, and there is a real chance VBUS is already being sourced because a warm reboot via macvdmtool does not power-cycle the PD controller, so a state left by macOS or by an earlier boot may persist. If a child DOES appear, that is a large shortcut and the next step is a READ-ONLY mount of the exFAT partition (ticket 109) -- no write without a fresh CJ approval. PASS/FAIL unchanged from the original plan: expected USB child persists 10 s, right DART/xHCI healthy, console responsive. Stop on SError, DART fault, role/power mismatch, lost console.
